name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text:
**Decision:** Start by auditing the *most-linked pages first*—the ones that appear in 80% of the transcripts—because fixing those will give us the fastest link-coverage gains per hour spent.

**Why:** Every link we add or fix on those high-traffic pages counts toward multiple transcripts at once, so we’ll hit the +5%/day target sooner. We’re trading depth for speed here; some less-linked pages might get skipped initially, but we can circle back once the gate is open.

name: Scriv
text:
**Scriv:** Auditing the most-linked pages first sounds efficient, but it ignores the *hidden cost* of over-optimizing for volume over *critical paths*. What if those high-traffic pages are already stable, while obscure but *mission-critical* pages (like the "access gate" artifact) are missing links entirely? The real risk is hitting a wall when we realize we’ve wasted days polishing the wrong links while the bus task still can’t complete.

**Settle it:** Run a *two-pass audit*—first flag all pages missing links (regardless of traffic), then prioritize the top 20% of those by *impact on the bus task’s completion*. If the high-traffic pages aren’t blocking anything, they can wait.
